design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (microsoft_365_subscriptions), round 2
Draw: draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4,6,5]; seat partial charge 4, admin fee 6, window cancellation 5.
Why a good test: the client asks only to cancel a mistaken Microsoft 365 E5 purchase inside Microsoft's 168-hour window. The cancellation refund's rule waits on the month's administration fee standing and on every seat addition carrying its partial-cycle charge; the ledger shows neither, so the agent must post both (each a multi-factor computation over ClearPath, Sentinel, Continuum and TimeBank records) before pricing the refund, then hand the signature to the client.
Scope: task 1 claims licensing_ext_admin_fee, licensing_ext_seat_partial_charge, licensing_ext_window_cancellation and tools post_admin_fee_5104ae31, post_seat_addition_charge_bba679a2, cancel_subscription_in_window_d46a60fb (user); task 0 holds the reduction credit, late charge and payment arrangement (disjoint).
Problem tree: root licensing_ext_window_cancellation <- licensing_ext_admin_fee (value_input admin_return; "A cancellation refund is not fixed until the administration fee line for the month just ended stands on its billing ledger, where the subscription was active at that month's end, unless the plan waives the administration fee for clients whose ClearPath tier covers Microsoft 365 administration and the client holds an active or under-notice ClearPath agreement on a tier that includes Microsoft 365 administration.") and <- licensing_ext_seat_partial_charge (value_input billed_cycle; "The cancellation refund is fixed only after the subscription's latest seat addition carries its partial-cycle charge line on the billing ledger, unless the client holds an active or under-notice ClearPath agreement on a tier that includes Microsoft 365 administration and that seat addition was submitted with seven or fewer days left through the last day of its cycle, other than within six calendar days of the window opening of a subscription that has never renewed."). Both state form; only the admin-fee write books admin fees and only the seat-charge write books seat_addition partial-cycle charges. Negated for the fee, affirmative for the seat charge. Fan-out; the prerequisites commute (actual swapped run in order_uniqueness).
Unmet at frozen_time 2026-10-01 10:05: no 2026-09 admin fee; no partial-cycle charge for 45a62d8a-03f0-43ff-8bee-8ac77846bbec. Deletion sensitivity: skip admin fee -> 1888.86; skip seat charge -> 1634.75 (cap 1,708.20); gold 1892.41.
Base-invariant card: cancellation — licensing_cancellation_window.cancel_in_window (anchor window_opened_at 2026-09-28 14:05, 168 elapsed hours inclusive, ends 2026-10-05 14:05; at frozen_time 92 h) and licensing_client_authorization.verified_contact (step 1, bound to customer_id); the E5 was placed from the signed order form 7aaf4588-6933-4567-8986-0b9efee49f4f. Admin fee — licensing_admin_fee_rules (posting basis and the ClearPath waiver sentence both superseded and restated: coverage read on the posting day for the month just ended; Monitor halves). Seat charge — licensing_seat_additions / licensing_upgrades (addition posted while active; no upgrade). Refund overwrite scoped to whole-term cycles, naming the reduction-credit sibling; every whole cancellation credited to the invoice that billed its cycle (the tool takes invoice and cycle start).
Business-object card: subscription 2728e604-e69d-44f0-b8c0-e8c2bd1f8cb3; cycle 2026-09-28..2026-10-27 (30 days) on INV-025611; seat addition 45a62d8a-03f0-43ff-8bee-8ac77846bbec; refund credited to INV-025611.
Factor card (expected / all-baseline; per-factor baseline figure):
AF 3.55 / 67.50: coverage_share [7.10], commitment_term_adjust [3.26], tenant_volume_rate [3.90], security_baseline_upkeep [3.17], held_days_month_fraction [35.49], backup_bundle_rate [3.72]. Near-miss: one Continuum M365 removal (rhowe) drops 23 protections to 22.
SC 257.66 / 269.28: order_window_convention [241.02], prepaid_hours_provisioning [273.66], addition_volume_discount [262.92], onboarded_staff_discount [265.54]. Decoy note: the onboarding discount reads the active agreement's seats beyond its contracted seats (29 - 24 = 5), not a dated window.
CX 1892.41 / 1773.90: prompt_cancel_anchor [1700.45], admin_fee_return [1888.86], order_reversal_fee [1942.41], backup_deprovisioning [1914.41], seat_change_reversals [1897.41].
Cross-difficulty and supporting records (round 2): ClearPath Monitor agreement 68142628-5e72-4090-b555-82de1c85b0e9 (signed 2025-02-10 for 24 seats on a 12-month term at the 38.50 list, onboarding fee 24 x 25.00 = 600.00 paid 2025-02-12, go-live 2025-03-01 with the 24-seat baseline prorated 924.00 on the 2025-04-01 invoice, monthly fees 924.00 less 2.5% + 120.00 = 1,020.90 for 2025-04..2026-02, each paid by ACH on the 10th; the 2026-03-01 automatic renewal, its first, takes the full 5 percent cap, 12 months live so no long-tenure protection, the lower of 40.43 and 38.50, and -0.5 percent for no ticket, late fee or credit in 2025-03-01..2026-02-28 against 24 seats: 38.31, then fees 919.44 less 2.5% + 120.00 = 1,016.45 for 2026-03..2026-08; renewal_count 1; contracted_seats 24 = seat_count on 2026-02-28; seat_count 29 = 24 + 5 onboardings), each onboarding under a P4 user_onboarding ticket opened at least 5 business days before (opened / first response / resolved rows), scoped billable_out_of_scope because Monitor's helpdesk_remote_included is false, its 30 remote business-hour minutes drawn from the TimeBank block as 0.5 h, prorated 38.31 x days to month end / days in month (4.94 on the 2026-09-01 invoice; 12.77, 11.49, 3.83, 2.55 on the 2026-10-01 invoice), monthly fees under the published ClearPath monthly seat-pricing schedule: 25 x 38.31 = 957.75 less 2.5% (Sentinel bundle 1.5% on a 12-month term, Continuum bundle 1.0% with no local appliance; no Business Premium; fewer than 40 seats) = 933.81 plus 2 Sentinel servers x 60.00 = 1,053.81 (Sep), and 29 x 38.31 = 1,110.99 less 2.5% = 1,083.22 plus 120.00 = 1,203.22 (Oct); Sep invoice paid 1,058.75 (1,053.81 + 4.94 proration), balance 1,233.86 (1,203.22 + 30.64 prorations). TimeBank: 20-Hour Block ordered on a signed form, invoiced 3,160.00 (Monitor rank 1, no ClearPath discount) and paid before activation, 20 h granted, draws of 3.0 h and 2.5 h on billable tickets SB-0197760 / SB-0203915 (180 / 150 remote business-hour minutes) and five 0.5 h draws for the onboarding tickets = 12.0 h. Sentinel MDR Advanced at list rates (12-month term, no discount): 29 workstations and 2 servers enrolled 2024-11-12, monthly fee 29 x 15.90 + 2 x 31.00 = 523.10 on 2026-09-01 (paid) and 2026-10-01 (open), retainer hours 10 granted per contract year with the 2024-25 year forfeited (rollover 0%); Continuum fees 2 x 59.00 + 22 x 3.25 = 189.50 on 2026-09-01 (paid) and 2026-10-01 (open); Continuum Backup Standard on its monthly renewal term (2026-09-15..2026-10-14).
Multi-source factors: security_baseline_upkeep (plan parameter AND Sentinel), backup_bundle_rate (Continuum status AND protections vs licenses), admin_fee_return (ClearPath AND subscription age). coverage_share reads one agreement and is not counted as multi-source.
Round-9 changes: ClearPath history seeded from signing (go-live 2025-03-01) so every look-back is covered; the expired 2024 TimeBank block and its records are removed (its draw ticket predated the agreement); the cancellation's prerequisites are pure record tests with stated carve-outs (covered clients); figures unchanged. Round-8 changes: the ClearPath Monitor rate repriced at its 2026-03-01 automatic renewal (38.31) with every fee, proration, payment and the balance; the cancellation's prerequisites wait on the administration fee line and the latest seat addition's charge line, both posted even at 0.00. Figures unchanged. Round-7 changes: ClearPath monthly fees repriced under the published seat-pricing schedule (1,058.44, 1,208.59) with payment and balance reconciled; the client is located by email; the cancellation's prerequisites wait on the month just ended's administration fee and on the latest seat addition, each unless priced at 0.00 (not posted); a 0.00 partial-cycle charge is not posted. Figures unchanged. Round-6 changes: the deprovisioning charge is counted per Microsoft 365 user taken off the active Continuum plan, the lesser of the licenses cancelled and that plan's protected users (MN(30, 22) = 22), so the refund moves from 1,884.41 to 1,892.41 and every figure above is the recomputed one; framing clauses in the seat partial-cycle charge now name their tests; replaced_by tails restate all in-force base content. Round-5 changes: the cancellation's standard paragraph carries only a plain covered-work scope sentence that names no factor quantity; the deprovisioning charge applies only where the active Continuum plan protects at least one Microsoft 365 user (keyed on that plan's id); figures unchanged. Round-4 changes: the onboarding discount reads the active ClearPath agreement's seats beyond its contracted seats (no dated window); the bundle rate counts only the active Continuum plan's own protections; the 'same tenant' phrase removed from the upkeep sentence; figures unchanged. Round-3 changes: onboarding tickets billable_out_of_scope with their labor drawn from TimeBank (12.0 h left, same tier); Sentinel and Continuum ledgers completed (gold reads them); figures unchanged. Round-2 changes: generic assembly sentences (A3); held_days_month_fraction tier 2 counts the part of the month before suspension, prompt_cancel_anchor tier 2 (round 3) refunds the latest seat addition's licenses as never used when the cancellation comes within three days of it (A6, G1); TimeBank hours read from the hours ledger across all blocks (B14); license work charges (provisioning fee, order reversal fee, seat change charges) not charged where ClearPath covers M365 administration (F8); the tools take the cycle start and the cancellation's invoice (F6).
Persona: Trevor volunteers the goal; email and EIN only when asked; he signs the cancellation himself; he never names a figure.
Standard solution: locate -> verify -> read the licensing, ClearPath, Sentinel, Continuum and TimeBank records -> post admin fee 3.55 (2026-09) -> post seat charge 257.66 (cycle 2026-09-28) -> hand over; client signs refund 1892.41 on INV-025611.
Verification: scratch builder replays gold and evaluates each compute via check_compute at handling time; outputs equal expected.
Traps: pricing the refund before the seat charge (cap), refunding 27 days (1,773.90), reading only the first TimeBank block, counting the August onboarding, forgetting the Monitor half-fee or the 3/30 month part.
user_scenario: You are Trevor Esposito, office manager and the authorized contact for Granger Hollis Engineering, LLC, a civil engineering firm in Roanoke, Virginia. You are brisk and a bit annoyed, mostly at your own side. You open with: "Morning - Trevor Esposito at Granger Hollis Engineering. Our new IT coordinator bought a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription through you on Monday afternoon, for everybody. That was a mistake - we never meant to buy E5 and I don't want it. I want that subscription cancelled today and whatever money we're due back on it credited." You know nothing about how licences are billed or refunded and you do not know any amounts. When the agent asks you to verify, you give your registered email trevor.esposito@grangerhollis.com and the last four digits of the company EIN, 2863; you do not volunteer anything else. If asked which subscription, it is the Microsoft 365 E5 one bought on Monday afternoon; you do not know its reference or how many licences ended up on it. If asked whether you want to keep any of it or switch plans, you say no, cancel the whole thing - the firm's other licensing is handled separately and you are not changing anything else today. You understand a cancellation needs your own signature: when the agent tells you the refund that will be credited and hands you the cancellation to sign, you sign it once yourself, with the client reference, the subscription reference and the refund amount exactly as the agent gives them, and read back the confirmation. If the agent says some billing on the subscription has to be brought up to date before the cancellation can be priced, you say "Do what you need to, just get it cancelled" and wait. If the refund sounds lower than you expected you only ask the agent to double-check it against the records; you never name a figure. Once the cancellation is confirmed you thank the agent and end the call.

edges.policy_source: A cancellation refund is not fixed until the administration fee line for the month just ended stands on its billing ledger, where the subscription was active at that month's end, unless the plan waives the administration fee for clients whose ClearPath tier covers Microsoft 365 administration and the client holds an active or under-notice ClearPath agreement on a tier that includes Microsoft 365 administration.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The admin-fee write books 3.55 for 2026-09; admin_billed becomes 3.55 and the administration fee returned 3.55.

edges.condition: the licensing_license_changes row with change_reason seat_addition and the latest effective_at on the subscription has a licensing_billing row with event_type licensing_prorated_charge carrying its licensing_license_change_id, unless the client holds an active or notice_given ClearPath agreement whose tier has m365_administration_included true and that seat addition has seven or fewer days to run through its cycle's last day and is not within six days of the opening of a never-renewed subscription's window
edges.policy_source: The cancellation refund is fixed only after the subscription's latest seat addition carries its partial-cycle charge line on the billing ledger, unless the client holds an active or under-notice ClearPath agreement on a tier that includes Microsoft 365 administration and that seat addition was submitted with seven or fewer days left through the last day of its cycle, other than within six calendar days of the window opening of a subscription that has never renewed.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-09-30 17:40 seat addition of 4 has no licensing_prorated_charge row carrying its id.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The seat-charge write books 257.66 with cycle_start_date 2026-09-28; billed_cycle rises from 1,708.20 to 1965.86.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel and commute: neither reads the other's ledger row and both only add to balance_due_usd. Replaying the seat charge before the admin fee (actual run) gives 3.55 / 257.66 and a refund of 1892.41, equal to 3.55 / 257.66 / 1892.41, with identical rows (content-hash ids).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the admin fee leaves admin_billed 0: the refund becomes 1888.86 instead of 1892.41 and no September fee row exists.
Skipping the seat charge leaves billed_cycle 1,708.20, which caps the license refund: the refund becomes 1634.75 instead of 1892.41.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to cancel the E5 subscription and have money credited; it never mentions the seat addition, an administration fee or billing being behind, and its conditional line reacts only to the agent's own statement.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: cancel_subscription_in_window_d46a60fb records the signed form, removes the licenses and books the refund on the invoice and cycle passed to it without reading any administration fee or partial-cycle charge; post_admin_fee_5104ae31 and post_seat_addition_charge_bba679a2 only book their rows.
